title: Non-defining relative clauses
titleVi: Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định
summary: Dấu phẩy đổi nghĩa câu, which thay cho cả mệnh đề, và cấu trúc many of whom.
whyItMatters: Ở band 8, câu của bạn cần thêm thông tin mà không chia thành câu mới — đó chính là việc của mệnh đề không xác định. Nhưng đặt thiếu dấu phẩy sẽ đổi nghĩa hoàn toàn: *The students who failed* là một nhóm, *The students, who failed,* là tất cả. Dùng *that* trong mệnh đề này là lỗi ngữ pháp rõ ràng, và dùng *which* để thay cho cả một ý là cấu trúc đặc trưng của văn học thuật.

sections.heading: Commas decide the meaning
body: A **defining** clause identifies which person or thing you mean: *The students who failed the exam had to retake it* (only some students failed). A **non-defining** clause adds extra information about something already identified: *The students, who failed the exam, had to retake it* (all of them failed).

The commas are not optional decoration. Written without them, the clause restricts; written with them, the clause comments. In academic writing this distinction carries real meaning, and misplacing a comma can invert your claim.
The same logic applies to proper nouns, which are already identified: *Hanoi, which is the capital, has a housing shortage* — never *Hanoi which is the capital*.

rows: The employees who work remotely save money.
The employees, who work remotely, save money.
My sister who lives in Da Nang is a nurse.
My sister, who lives in Da Nang, is a nurse.
The report which was leaked caused a scandal.
The report, which was leaked, caused a scandal.
People who drive to work face higher costs.
Commuting, which many people do daily, is expensive.

sections.heading: No that, no omission
body: Non-defining clauses use **who, which, whose, where, when, whom** — but never **that**. *The policy, that was introduced in 2019, failed* is wrong; use *which*.

The pronoun cannot be omitted either, because it is the only signal that a clause is coming: *The policy, introduced in 2019, failed* is acceptable only as a reduced participial phrase, not as a full clause.

The clause sits between two commas (or a comma and a full stop) and can be removed without breaking the sentence. Test it: if the sentence still works after deleting the clause, the commas belong there.

examples.right: The minister, who resigned last week, denied the allegations.
examples.wrong: The minister, that resigned last week, denied the allegations.
examples.note: Không dùng **that** trong mệnh đề không xác định.

examples.right: The scheme, which cost £2 million, was abandoned.
examples.note: Có thể bỏ cả mệnh đề mà câu vẫn hoàn chỉnh.

examples.right: Researchers, whose funding was cut, had to scale back the trial.
examples.note: **whose** hoạt động bình thường trong mệnh đề không xác định.

sections.heading: which referring to a whole clause
body: In non-defining clauses, **which** can refer not to a noun but to the entire previous clause. This is a compact way to comment on a fact: *The trial was cancelled, which surprised the participants.* *Fares rose by 40%, which made commuting unaffordable for many.*
The related structure **in which case** is even tighter: *The deadline may be extended, in which case we should revise the schedule.*
Use this device sparingly — two or three times in an essay. Overused, it produces the loose, trailing sentences that examiners describe as under-controlled.

rows: Enrolment fell by half, which forced the college to close.
The data were incomplete, which is why the report was delayed.
The grant may be renewed, in which case we can expand.
Fewer than 10% responded, a fact that weakens the conclusion.

sections.heading: Quantifier + of whom / of which
body: To talk about a part of a group already mentioned, use a quantifier plus **of whom** (people) or **of which** (things): *Twenty candidates applied, only three of whom were shortlisted.* *The city has ten districts, most of which are overcrowded.*
This structure is a band-8 marker because it packs two ideas into one sentence without a conjunction. It replaces *and only three of them were shortlisted*, which is looser.
Note that the pronoun is obligatory: *most of them are* becomes *most of which are*. Dropping it — *ten districts, most are overcrowded* — produces a comma splice.

examples.right: The survey covered 400 households, half of whom lived in rented flats.
examples.wrong: The survey covered 400 households, half of them lived in rented flats.
examples.note: Cần **of whom** để nối thành mệnh đề quan hệ.

examples.right: The library holds 200,000 volumes, many of which are out of print.
Several factors, none of which is decisive, explain the trend.
examples.note: Số ít sau *none of which* trong văn trang trọng.

sections.heading: Reduction and the appositive alternative
body: Non-defining clauses reduce to participial phrases: *The report, which was published in May, ...* → *The report, published in May, ...*; *The students, who were waiting outside, ...* → *The students, waiting outside, ...*
An **appositive** — a noun phrase in commas — often does the same job more elegantly: *Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam, ...* rather than *Hanoi, which is the capital of Vietnam, ...*
In Task 1, prefer appositives and reduced clauses; in Task 2, one full non-defining clause per paragraph is enough to demonstrate the structure without bloating sentences.

examples.right: The bridge, completed in 2010, carries 40,000 vehicles a day.
examples.note: Rút gọn bị động — gọn hơn *which was completed*.

examples.right: Da Nang, Vietnam's third-largest city, relies heavily on tourism.
examples.note: Appositive thay cho *which is the third-largest city*.

examples.right: The policy failed, which undermined public trust in the ministry.
examples.note: Một mệnh đề *which* đủ mạnh; không cần thêm mệnh đề thứ hai.

commonMistakes.wrong: My father, that works in Hanoi, comes home at weekends.
commonMistakes.right: My father, who works in Hanoi, comes home at weekends.
commonMistakes.why: Mệnh đề **không xác định không dùng *that***. Với người phải dùng **who**, với vật dùng **which**.

commonMistakes.wrong: Hanoi, where I visited last year, has changed a lot.
commonMistakes.right: Hanoi, which I visited last year, has changed a lot.
commonMistakes.why: **where** thay cho cụm trạng ngữ chỉ nơi chốn, không thay cho tân ngữ. *Visit* cần tân ngữ nên phải dùng **which**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The scheme which cost two million pounds was abandoned.
commonMistakes.right: The scheme, which cost two million pounds, was abandoned.
commonMistakes.why: Thiếu cặp dấu phẩy khiến câu thành mệnh đề xác định — nghĩa đổi thành *chỉ kế hoạch tốn hai triệu mới bị hủy*, trong khi ý là thông tin bổ sung.

commonMistakes.wrong: The report, which it was published in May, was criticised.
commonMistakes.right: The report, which was published in May, was criticised.
commonMistakes.why: Đại từ quan hệ đã là chủ ngữ của mệnh đề, nên không thêm *it*. Đây là lỗi lặp chủ ngữ giống *the book which I bought it*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The city has ten districts, most of them are overcrowded.
commonMistakes.right: The city has ten districts, most of which are overcrowded.
commonMistakes.why: Hai mệnh đề chính nối bằng dấu phẩy là lỗi *comma splice*. Cần đại từ quan hệ **most of which** để biến vế sau thành mệnh đề phụ.

ieltsTips: Dùng `..., which is why...` để nêu hệ quả trong Task 2: `Few households recycle, which is why landfill sites are filling up.`
Trong Task 1, dùng `..., most of which...` / `..., half of whom...` để gộp số liệu vào một câu thay vì liệt kê.
Rút gọn mệnh đề không xác định thành cụm phân từ: `The study, conducted in 2021, found...` — ngắn hơn và đúng band 8.
Chỉ dùng một hoặc hai mệnh đề `which` trong cả bài; dùng quá nhiều sẽ bị đánh giá là câu thiếu kiểm soát.

exercises.question: The minister, ___ resigned last week, has denied the allegations.
exercises.explanation: Mệnh đề không xác định, chỉ người → **who** (không dùng *that*).

exercises.question: The bridge, ___ was completed in 2010, carries 40,000 vehicles a day.
exercises.explanation: Chỉ vật trong mệnh đề không xác định → **which**.

exercises.question: Fares rose by 40%, ___ made commuting unaffordable for many.
exercises.explanation: **which** thay cho cả mệnh đề phía trước.

exercises.question: Twenty candidates applied, only three of ___ were shortlisted.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: My sister who lives in Da Nang is a nurse.
My sister, who lives in Da Nang, is a nurse.
My sister, who lives in Da Nang is a nurse.
My sister who lives in Da Nang, is a nurse.
exercises.explanation: Mệnh đề bổ sung thông tin cần **cặp dấu phẩy** đầy đủ.

exercises.question: The library holds 200,000 volumes, many of ___ are out of print.
The deadline may be extended, in ___ case we should revise the schedule.
Da Nang, ___ is Vietnam's third-largest city, relies on tourism.
exercises.explanation: **which** — không dùng *that* trong mệnh đề không xác định.

exercises.question: Few households recycle, ___ is why landfill sites are filling up.
exercises.explanation: **which is why** nối hệ quả với cả mệnh đề trước.
